lines.x: The workload's as heavy as ever today, Doctor. Don't worry—I'll get through it with you.

By now that lot in my squad have surely made some new mess for me. Never mind—a day without the racket would feel wrong, honestly. Besides, without those noisy brats there'd be nothing to set a quiet life against—yes, I know. Telling myself that makes it a little easier.

Lately a lot of people tell me I give off a completely different impression since I changed my outfit. The real reason lies elsewhere, but I don't mind. Come to think of it, a change of clothes really does change your image. Care to try, Doctor? I'll design one for you free of charge.

Come spring, I'm thinking of taking the squad to Higashi to see the bamboo groves there. Of course no country called the 'Bubbly Realm' will be waiting for us. It's just... I've started to miss the sound of wind through bamboo leaves.

Come to think of it, that lot cause trouble every day, but they do finish everything I hand them—eventually, after enough dawdling. Maybe there's no need to be so hard on them... No. I can't go soft on them. Spot! This report is a mess. Rewrite it!

Popukar, what is it? ...Midnight and Spot snuck off to train again? I know. It's probably because Catapult and I have been training so much lately—it's made them anxious. Ugh, that stupid pride of theirs. Well, not my problem. Come on, let's go bring them a midnight snack.

I've been wondering—maybe Dr. Kal'tsit put me in charge of A6 from the start because she saw right through me. She knew that whatever I say out loud, I can't actually leave the people beside me to fend for themselves. Oh, am I that easy to read? Hah. Doctor, you can deal with this stack of paperwork yourself.

Midnight takes so many things seriously. Catapult pours everything she has into what she loves. Spot has his own pride. Popukar is thoughtful and capable. I keep thinking more people ought to see those sides of them. But then... maybe it's enough that I know.

Care for a slice, Doctor? The kids made this cake. I've already tried it—for beginners, it's not bad at all. I have no idea when they learned to do that behind my back. I'm always saying A6 can't last forever... and yet I've nearly lost count of how many years we've been together.
You're quite the free spirit yourself, Doctor. Never mind—there's nothing about you for me to worry over anyway.

I conquered a foreign king and his general, then led the squad to slay a giant monster? Tch. Catapult, you just wait. ...No, I can't say she's making it up, exactly. It's just—ugh, where do I even begin...
Oh no—where did that archery tutorial I saved go?!
Dobermann says I've been coming to the training grounds more often lately? ...No. It's just that drawing a bow demands complete concentration, so it forces me to stop dwelling on all sorts of things.

Given the choice between taking up a weapon against beasts and taking up a pen against paperwork, I'd still pick the pen. Ah, life never does go the way you want. Still, my design sketches have been coming out more smoothly lately—I suppose that counts as a good thing.
I've already read the mission briefing. Leave it to me.
Then I'll assign the operation's tasks.
I've checked the logistics supplies. No problems—let's move out.
Carry out the mission as planned. There's no need to panic.
Shall we hold a briefing?
I have a few ideas. Want to talk them over?
I've already spotted their weak point.
Let's finish quickly. There's a mountain of work waiting back home.
Wirebug, I'm counting on you.
Set the work aside for a moment...
Focus everything on what's in front of me...
I prepared for a situation like this long ago.
Every time I finish a mission like this, I think the same thing: challenges like these don't suit me. For me, holding on to my own little corner of the world is enough.
Tally the losses, report the wounded... Doctor, leave the tedious parts to me. I'm something of an expert at this by now.
Don't worry, Doctor. Our losses are minimal—we can still press the pursuit.
I really am no good at this fighting business, am I.
I've gotten used to the noise here, too.
Hold on—stop tugging my sleeve!
Doctor, that's it for today's work. We're clocking out!
Arknights.

Popukar, why have you turned into a tree? Midnight, where did this champagne tower come from? Catapult, this is a New Year's party, not a trophy exhibition! And Spot, please stop projecting comics on the wall—Fine, I admit it. I never should have let you decorate the place yourselves.
Doctor, is there anything you need help with?

Happy birthday, Doctor. I sewed you a charm, with a little piece of the 'firebamboo charcoal' I brought back from the 'Bubbly Realm' tucked inside. Write down your birthday wish and slip it in—who knows, it might just come true.

There isn't much good in my past. Coming to Rhodes Island and finding Squad A6 counts as one of the few. Something invisible and intangible—but undeniably real—tied us together. I keep saying that one day we're bound to part ways. But the one who can't let this squad go... might just be me.
